plan.why: Its pages talk straight to Supabase, so llocal gives it a small server of its own, written in Go, and keeps the data in SQLite.
found: A React website, made with Bolt.
A Supabase database at qrstuvwxyzabcdefghij.supabase.co, with 1 table: quotes. Visitors' browsers talk to it directly.
Its own login: email and password through Supabase, with people kept in auth.users.

left.text: It has its own login (email and password through Supabase), which goes: llocal's sign-in takes its place.
Its data is in Supabase (1 table) and moves into one SQLite file beside the app.
Visitors' browsers talk to Supabase directly. Those calls go through the app's own server instead.
It has no server of its own, and needs a small one in Go, on llocal's kit, for the work Supabase does for its pages.
A secret key sits in its pages, where anyone can read it (VITE_OPENAI_API_KEY). It moves to the server, and needs replacing with a new one.
It has no llocal.json yet: the short file that tells llocal how to build and start it.

changes.text: The Supabase data moves into one SQLite file on llocal, copied over once.
changes.detail: SQLite sits right next to the app, so it is fast, it is backed up with the app, and only people who can open the app reach the data.

changes.text: The pages stop talking to the database directly and ask the app's own server instead.
changes.detail: Today each visitor's browser reaches the database with a key anyone can read in the pages, and only the database's own rules stand in the way. On llocal only people who have signed in reach the data, and only through the server, which checks the same rules.

changes.text: The app's own login goes, and llocal signs people in.
changes.detail: People sign in with llocal, and nobody keeps another password. You choose who can open the app. The list of people in auth.users stays, so everyone keeps their own records.

changes.text: llocal adds a small server, written in Go, that does the work Supabase did for the pages.
changes.detail: A Go server starts in a moment and needs little memory, so the app is quick and can sleep when nobody is using it.

outside.detail: It needs OPENAI_API_KEY. Visitors' browsers talk to it directly.

needs.text: Your OpenAI key, saved as OPENAI_API_KEY.

So llocal can copy your data once: a key that can read every table of your Supabase project (qrstuvwxyzabcdefghij.supabase.co). The service_role key (Supabase > Project Settings > API Keys) or the database password will do. It is used for the copy, then thrown away.

warnings: VITE_OPENAI_API_KEY looks like a secret key, and anything named VITE_... is copied into the pages every visitor downloads, where anyone can read it. Make a new one at the service and stop using this one; llocal keeps the new one on the server as a secret.

settings.name: OPENAI_API_KEY
settings.note: Was VITE_OPENAI_API_KEY, in the pages. llocal moves what uses it to the server, so it can stay secret.
settings.warning: VITE_OPENAI_API_KEY looks like a secret key, and anything named VITE_... is copied into the pages every visitor downloads, where anyone can read it. Make a new one at the service and stop using this one; llocal keeps the new one on the server as a secret.

plan.if_not_converted: Until it is converted, the Supabase database is reached straight from each visitor's browser, and llocal's sign-in does not stand in front of it: anyone who has its address and the key in the pages can try to read it.
